belief: If I am suffering, God is punishing me.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you are suffering God is punishing you, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that every hardship is God’s punishment for sin. Friends who asked, “What did you do to deserve this?” A guilty conscience that looks for reasons. Childhood punishment that taught you pain always means you did wrong. Wanting an explanation for suffering.
teaches: Sometimes suffering is a natural consequence of sin, and God does lovingly discipline His children for their good. But Scripture does not teach that all suffering is punishment. Job was blameless, yet he suffered greatly, and God rebuked the friends who said it was his fault. Jesus said the man born blind did not suffer because of anyone’s sin. For believers, the punishment for sin fell on Jesus. Suffering is part of living in a broken world, and God is with you in it.
self_statements: God is punishing me for something.
I must have done something to deserve this.
This pain proves God is angry with me.
If I were living right, this wouldn’t happen.
I have to figure out what sin caused this.
errors: Assuming suffering is always about something you did.
Turning “sin can bring consequences” into “all suffering is punishment.”
Picturing God as eager to punish.
questions: What did Jesus say about the man born blind?
Was Job suffering because of his sin?
What did God say to Job’s friends who blamed him?
Where did the punishment for my sin go, according to Isaiah 53:5?
Is there a clear sin I need to confess, or am I searching for a reason?
What does Lamentations 3:33 say about God’s heart?
Can I trust God’s love even in my suffering?
truth: My suffering does not automatically mean God is punishing me. Job suffered though he was blameless, and Jesus said the blind man’s condition was not caused by sin. For those in Christ, the punishment for sin fell on Jesus. God may discipline me for my good, but He does not willingly afflict me. He is with me in my suffering.
hw_questions: What did Jesus say about the man born blind?
Was Job suffering for his sin?
What did God say to Job’s friends?
Am I searching for a reason that isn’t there?
What is God’s heart toward my suffering?
hw_truths: Jesus took the punishment for my sin.
God does not willingly afflict me.
God’s discipline is for my good, not my destruction.
God is with me in my suffering.
log: Each day, write one hard thing and one way God showed care or presence in it.
name_example: For the Lord will not cast Sarah off forever. Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion. For He does not willingly afflict or grieve her.
actions: and write what the friends got wrong about Job’s suffering.
If there is a clear sin, confess it once,
then stop searching for hidden reasons.
and write how Jesus responded to suffering.
Talk with a pastor or Christian counselor
about your suffering and your fears.
tracker: One sign of God’s care in suffering
prayer: Father, I am suffering, and I don’t understand why. Help me reject the lie that You are punishing me. Thank You that Jesus took my punishment and that You do not willingly afflict me. Be near to me in this hard time and show me Your compassion. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
